verified_loci: Merivale: From Sappho. A Fragment (1813) — 'ADDITIONAL EPIGRAMS. 1813. FROM SAPPHO. A FRAGMENT. Blest as the immortal Gods is he,'
Merivale's fr. 31, its close at the failing of sight and sound — 'I grow ; and then — together fail Both sight and sound !'
why_seated: Merivale's fr. 31 in four stanzas that end at the failing of sight and sound, one of the renderings Wharton reprints (v7 §5.3).
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-11-07: "i think we need a sappho reception history ea-corpora, whatever's public. translators, scholars. theres some ground work in the archive, notes towards a future reader i believe. the seating can include everything thats publicly available as well as declared absences and pointers for material behind pay- and access- and rights-walls"; and: "sappho reception history + future reader frameworks and related"; and at 12:47 EST, of the first draft: "this seems light on scholarly material related to the future reader proposition or sappho... and that is the focus of notes towards a future reader, is it not?"
research: The revision of Closing the Fragment (v7, a draft of 2026-11-07 for Alexanarch), whose §6 controls the January composition against the translators from Hall (1652) to Carson and whose §8 declares an exposure-checked panel; and the Sappho Future Reader framework, whose groundwork is Research Notes Towards the Future Reader (#1548: Part I the scholarly field, Part II the future reader in twelve strata), and whose reading by a signed-out ChatGPT on 2026-11-07 is seated as capture 0C3D (sappho-future-reader-framework-constitutive-materials-chatgpt-20261107).
